_comment: Worst-of countdowns ('Most Polluted Air', 'Most Corrupt Countries', ...) for the rotating series' 'worst' day (daily_variation.SERIES_CYCLE). Same schema and the same never-invent-a-number pipeline as config/rankings_metrics.json, kept in a separate file so the daily rankings rotation is untouched. Live metrics come from the World Bank API; the static ones read the BOTTOM of the same published tables the daily series reads from the top (config/rankings_static.json *_bottom blocks, refreshed monthly with the others). 'countdown_phrase' is what follows 'counting down the N ...' when the raw index name would read backwards (counting down 'by Corruption Perceptions Index' from the lowest score). tone 'serious': these are facts about real people's lives -- stated plainly, never mocked. Rotation is one metric per 'worst' day, in this order; append new metrics at the end.

metrics.label: PM2.5 Air Pollution
metrics.countdown_phrase: countries with the most polluted air
metrics.note: PM2.5 is the yearly average of fine particles in the air people breathe, in micrograms per cubic metre, and higher means dirtier air

metrics.label: Corruption Perceptions Index
metrics.countdown_phrase: countries seen as the most corrupt
metrics.note: on the Corruption Perceptions Index a LOWER score means MORE corrupt, and it measures how corrupt the public sector is perceived to be

metrics.label: Inflation Rate
metrics.note: this is the yearly rise in consumer prices

metrics.label: World Happiness Score
metrics.note: the score is how people rate their own lives from 0 to 10, so a LOWER score means people are less happy

metrics.label: Total Greenhouse Gas Emissions
metrics.countdown_phrase: countries emitting the most greenhouse gases
metrics.note: these are TOTAL national emissions, so large economies and large populations rank high

metrics.label: Democracy Index
metrics.note: the Democracy Index scores countries from 0 to 10, and a LOWER score means less democratic

metrics.label: Unemployment Rate
metrics.note: this is the share of the labour force without work, as estimated by the International Labour Organization

metrics.label: Homicide Rate
metrics.countdown_phrase: countries with the highest murder rates
metrics.note: this counts intentional homicides per 100,000 people
